messages.content: Which neighborhoods in Florianópolis are best for a foreigner renting for six months? I want safe, walkable, near a beach, with fast internet.

For a six-month stay that balances safety, walkability, and beach access, your best options depend on whether you want a social expat hub or a high-end, secure enclave.

## Top Neighborhood Recommendations

**Lagoa da Conceição** — This is the primary choice for international living [7]. It serves as the epicenter of international life, allowing you to live for months without needing Portuguese [7]. It is highly walkable, with supermarkets, bars, and coworking spaces all within walking distance [7].

**Jurerê Internacional** — This is the best option if you have a higher budget and prioritize maximum safety [7]. It features patrolled streets, open lawns, and gorgeous parks [7]. It has a safety score of 78/100 and reported zero robberies in 2025, though a one-bedroom here can cost around €1,200/month as of May 2026 [1].

**Centro** — If walkability is your absolute priority, the city center is the exception in a city that isn't naturally pedestrian-friendly [3]. You can spend days here without needing a car [3]. While not a beach neighborhood, it offers excellent central infrastructure [3].

## Comparison of Key Factors

| Neighborhood | Primary Vibe | Safety/Walkability Profile |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Lagoa da Conceição** | International/Social | Everything is within walking distance [7]. |
| **Jurerê Internacional** | High-end/Secure | Maximum safety; zero reported robberies in 2025 [1][7]. |
| **Centro** | Urban/Functional | The best walkability in the city [3]. |

## Infrastructure and Logistics

**Internet** — You will not struggle with connectivity in the central neighborhoods. Fiber optic service providing 300 to 500 Mbps typically runs R$100 to R$150/month [2]. While internet is reliable in central areas, the real differentiator for remote work is often the pace of daily life rather than raw bandwidth [2].

**Transportation** — Be aware that Florianópolis is not a pedestrian-centric city by design [3]. If you choose a neighborhood that isn't a central hub, you may face a 40-minute commute to find good coffee or specific amenities [3]. Choosing a neighborhood that doesn't match your lifestyle could lead to isolation or connectivity issues [3].

**Cost-Saving Tip** — If you are looking to lower your rental costs, Canasvieiras sees rental prices drop to a minimum during the off-season (April to November) [7]. In this area, it is recommended to secure a yearly contract rather than a short 3-month lease [7].
